title: Show claim, blocked work, and review status in the TUI
lead: The queue status column is seven characters, so `reviewing` overflows. A blocked review or parked row has no `!`. Review uses the normal color. The detail pane does not show the claim.
findings_note: user request: the TUI cannot show who has a slice, and review rows are easy to miss
boundary: **Not in this slice:** a claim column on the queue row; the `v` view cycle (s165); handoff, reject, and release keys.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: Someone looking at the queue cannot tell a ready review from ordinary open work, and cannot tell a blocked review from an unblocked one. The detail pane is where the claim owner fits. The half-width queue is already too narrow for another column. s165 owns the view key.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/tui.py` (row layout, blocked marker, detail pane)
- `src/slicer/tui_style.py` (a review role)
- `docs/tui.md`
- `tests/test_tui.py`
- `CHANGELOG.md`

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
1. The detail pane shows the claim owner, or `-` when the item has none.
2. The status column is as wide as the longest visible label, and a `reviewing` row stays aligned with a `started` row.
3. A blocked review row and a blocked parked row show `!`. An unblocked row does not.
4. `review_status` uses a role that is not the started role and not the parked role. With no spare color pair, that role is bold. The status word is still drawn. `NO_COLOR` stays monochrome.
5. The queue row has no claim column, and `v` is not bound by this slice.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body: Widen the status column from the visible labels. Mark every blocked visible row. Add the claim line to the detail pane. Give the review status its own role, using a spare color pair when the terminal has one and bold otherwise. Do not add a queue claim column or a view binding.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: The failing tests pass, then `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests`, `slicer check`, and `git diff --check`.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch, including the re-rendered roadmap and a CHANGELOG entry under Unreleased.
